source_note: Topic structure follows the OCR A-Level History A specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

connections.why: The early and later Tudor period studies are consecutive halves of the same dynasty's reign
Elizabethan government's tensions feed directly into the early Stuart crisis
The Tudor period study supplies the political context for the thematic study of Tudor rebellion and disorder
Elizabethan domestic study pairs with the thematic survey of Tudor foreign policy
Henry VII bridges the Wars of the Roses and the founding of the Tudor state
The Russia 1894–1941 period study sits inside the long thematic study of Russia and its rulers
Early Romanov rule is the starting point for the broad survey of Russia's rulers
Westward expansion and the Civil War set up the long fight over civil rights in the USA
The German Reformation provokes the Catholic Reformation studied thematically
Reformation ideas grew out of the intellectual ferment of the Renaissance
Spain under Ferdinand, Isabella and Charles V leads straight into the reign of Philip II
Unification creates the liberal state that fascism later overturns
Italian and German unification are parallel nineteenth-century nationalist movements
The fall of Napoleon opens the restored and Second Empire France of 1814–1870
The European and Asian Cold Wars are two theatres of the same superpower conflict
Divided Germany is the central front of the Cold War in Europe
Interwar diplomacy explains the rise of the dictatorships studied in Germany
The growth of empire to 1783 and its later dismantling form one continuous imperial story
The expansion of Islam created the world the Crusades later contested
Crusader conflict in the Levant prefigures the rise of Ottoman power there
Ottoman ascendancy and decline frame the modern Middle East and the Arab Spring
The Norman Conquest period study shares the post-1066 crown-and-Church theme
Anglo-Saxon England is reshaped by the Viking raids and settlement that follow
The source-enquiry skills of the British study underpin the evidence-based NEA essay
Working with rival interpretations in the thematic study models the historiography the NEA demands
